kicker: Basic to pro, one rung at a time
headline: Start on the free tool. Climb to the one that pays.
intro: Every niche has a ladder: the free tool you can open today, the workhorse clients expect, and the paid tool that sets your rate apart. You don't buy your way up, you build your way up. Each rung leaves you a real portfolio piece.
creed: Nobody gets hired for owning a tool. They get hired for what they built with it. So climb one real piece at a time.
tiersNote: Three rungs per niche. Most rungs have a genuine free tier or a trial long enough to build one real piece, so the only thing between you and the next rung is the work.

howItWorks.meaning: The free tool you can open today. No card, no excuse. This rung proves you can produce clean, usable work at all.
The workhorse clients expect you to know. Usually a generous free tier or a trial long enough to build one real piece.
The paid, premium tool that separates a hire from an applicant. Learn it on a trial, then charge for it once a client is paying.

ladder.goal: You can run a founder's calendar and inbox so they never have to think about the logistics.

tools.name: Google Workspace
tools.free: Free on a personal Google account; paid per user for orgs
tools.what: Run calendar, inbox, docs, and files

tools.name: Calendly
tools.free: Free plan, one active event type
tools.what: Share a booking link, end scheduling ping-pong

ladder.piece: A color-coded weekly calendar and a Calendly booking link for a mock founder, plus a one-page daily brief.

ladder.goal: You can turn how a founder works into written systems the whole team can follow.

tools.name: Notion
tools.free: Free plan, unlimited pages for solo use
tools.what: Build SOPs, wikis, and meeting-prep docs

tools.name: Slack
tools.free: Free plan, last 90 days of history

ladder.piece: An SOP library in Notion: 3-5 written processes (inbox triage, meeting prep, travel booking) with a reusable meeting-prep template.

ladder.piece: A founder operations hub: a full travel itinerary and briefing packet, a documented access plan, and a Loom walkthrough of the week ahead.
